SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - FICTIONAL PATIENT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
COLONOSCOPY REPORT
Facility: Ashford Valley Endoscopy (fictional)
Patient: Lorraine Petrakis (fictional)
Date of service: November 5, 2026
Endoscopist: Desmond Achebe-Rowe, MD (fictional)
Indication: Abdominal pain and change in bowel habit.
Procedure: The colonoscope was advanced to the cecum, confirmed by the appendiceal orifice.
Findings:
- Descending colon: a 6 mm sessile polyp, removed completely with a cold snare and retrieved.
- Hepatic flexure: a 10 mm sessile polyp on the proximal side of a thick fold.
- Snare removal of this polyp was attempted, but the snare could not be positioned around it.
- The hepatic flexure polyp was not removed, and no tissue was taken from it.
- The remainder of the colon was normal.
Impression:
1. 6 mm descending colon polyp, removed by cold snare.
2. 10 mm hepatic flexure polyp, not removed after a failed snare attempt.
Plan: Repeat colonoscopy with a distal cap in 4 to 6 weeks to remove the hepatic flexure polyp.
